outcomes.text: Students will be able to recognize various ICT devices and their applications.
Students will be able to define and differentiate between computer hardware and software.
Students will be able to identify and analyze (basic) hardware components of a computing system (e.g. processor, memory and storage).

subtopics.title: Operating systems, image processing and the internet

outcomes.text: Students will be able to navigate around an Operating System (e.g. Microsoft Windows, MAC OS, Linux, Ubuntu, Android, iOS, etc).

Students will be able to develop and demonstrate image-processing skills (using various software tools e.g. Paint, 3D Paint, Tux, etc.), while efficiently using computer hardware (e.g. mouse, keyboard, etc.)
Students will demonstrate how to navigate the internet to conduct a search query and arrive at an authentic result.

units.title: Domain C: Algorithmic Thinking and Problem Solving

topics.title: Domain C: Algorithmic Thinking and Problem Solving

subtopics.title: Defining problems and basic algorithmic thinking

outcomes.text: Students will be able to identify, define and analyze a problem
Students will be able to apply basic algorithmic thinking to solve different types of problems.
Students will be able to analyze the fundamentals of computer programming.

Students will be able to analyze and apply basic programming constructs (e.g. sequence, selection, repetition, variables, inputs/events); by creating simple single-sprite, single-script programs using a visual programming tool.

Additional SLO: Students will be able to apply basic programming constructs (e.g. sequence, selection, repetition, variables, inputs/events); by creating simple single-sprite, single-script programs using textual programming tools.
Students will analyze the basics of information literacy and digital civility and appropriate uses of technology.

units.title: Domain F: Entrepreneurship in Digital Age

topics.title: Domain F: Entrepreneurship in Digital Age

outcomes.text: Students will define and analyze entrepreneurship subtypes and summarize the entrepreneurship process

Students will be able to identify the use of emerging technologies in various walks of life (e.g. artificial intelligence, biometrics, robotics, computer-assisted translation, 3D and holographic imaging, virtual reality, Cloud Computing, and open-source software.
Students will be able to identify (advanced) hardware components of a computing system (e.g. different types of I/O ports, different types of peripherals, and networking components).
Students will be able to develop and demonstrate word-processing and presentation skills (using various software tools e.g. MS Word, MS PowerPoint, Prezi, Canva, Photo Story, Movie-maker, etc.)
Students will get introduced to electronic mailing systems (e-mail) and learn appropriate usage.

units.title: Domain C: Algorithmic Thinking and Problem Solving

topics.title: Domain C: Algorithmic Thinking and Problem Solving

outcomes.text: Students will be able to apply the concept of computational thinking to handle complex problems.
Students will be able to apply concepts of conditional statements, finite and infinite loops to write different algorithms.
Students will be able to explain how computers encode and decode computer programs (i.e. identification of decimal to binary and vice versa, conversion of texts, images and sounds in binary).
Students will be able to apply fundamental programming constructs to create multi-sprite, multi-script programs using visual programming tools.
Additional SLO: Students will be able to apply fundamental programming constructs to create multi-sprite, multi-script programs using textual programming tools.
Students will identify ways to protect against malicious activities or behaviors in the digital environment.

units.title: Domain F: Entrepreneurship in Digital Age

topics.title: Domain F: Entrepreneurship in Digital Age

outcomes.text: Students will analyze the uses and benefits of design thinking for entrepreneurs.

Students will be able to analyze the usage of emerging technologies in various walks of life (e.g. artificial intelligence, 5G, robotics, computer-assisted translation, 3D and holographic imaging, virtual reality, distributed applications, block-chain, and Machine Learning.)
Students will be able to identify and analyze a network and identify core networking components and their roles.
Students will be able to develop and demonstrate data handling skills (using various software tools e.g. MS Excel, Google sheets, etc.)
Additional SLO: Students will learn how to research information from the internet for a report that answers a research question and communicates results and conclusions.

units.title: Domain C: Algorithmic Thinking and Problem Solving

topics.title: Domain C: Algorithmic Thinking and Problem Solving

outcomes.text: Students will be able to apply the concepts of computational thinking and problem-solving strategies to solve complex problems by identifying the most efficient algorithm
Students will be able to apply the concepts of nesting in algorithmic design thinking.
Students will be able to apply intermediate-level programming constructs (e.g. functions, cloning, conditional movement); by creating mini-games using a visual programming tool.
Additional SLO: Students will be able to apply intermediate-level programming constructs (e.g. functions, cloning, conditional movement); by creating mini-games using a textual programming tool.
Students will identify ways of protecting against cybercrimes.

units.title: Domain F: Entrepreneurship in Digital Age

topics.title: Domain F: Entrepreneurship in Digital Age

outcomes.text: Students will develop an understanding of the basics of digital marketing platforms and social media marketing to develop a marketing plan for a business.
Students will be able to identify and create different components of a business plan i.e. market need, product design, costing, operations, and marketing.
Students will define and describe types of systems (artificial, natural), computer hardware components such as computer architecture (CPU, microprocessors, etc.),
Students will be able to identify and explain system software, application software, low-level and high-level programming languages, and their uses.

Students will be able to identify and analyze data communication, computer networks, networking devices, basic networking systems and understand how data is transmitted and key concepts such as protocols, speeds, etc.
Understand and apply techniques to decompose problems
Solve simple and complex problems computationally
Students will understand web development and differentiate between a website and a web application
Students should be able to create a static website using HTML/CSS in an appropriate environment
Students should be able to create dynamic websites using JavaScript as the frontend scripting
Students should be able to implement common algorithms that use sequence, selection, and repetition in JavaScript
Students will determine ways of debugging their code in JavaScript

subtopics.title: Data science, data types and big data

outcomes.text: Students will explain the scope of the data science field as an interdisciplinary field (computer sciences, mathematics & statistics, and business knowledge & understanding).
Students will define and explain data types, data collection, and data storage.
Students will be able to define and explain big data, and applications of big data in real-world business

units.title: Domain E: Applications of Computer Science

topics.title: Domain E: Applications of Computer Science

subtopics.title: AI, machine learning and cloud computing

outcomes.text: Students will be able to describe uses and applications of computing like AI, Machine Learning, and Cloud Computing
Students will be able to discuss the social implication of the usage of AI in decision-making that affects humans

subtopics.title: Safe use and impacts of computing

outcomes.text: Understand and apply safe and responsible use of computers (responsible use of hardware, appropriate use of software, and safe use of digital platforms like data searches, social networking, etc.)
Analyze the beneficial and harmful effects of computing innovations such as social networking, fake news, etc.
Evaluate the ways computing impacts personal, ethical, social, economic, and cultural practices

units.title: Domain H: Entrepreneurship in the Digital Age

topics.title: Domain H: Entrepreneurship in the Digital Age

outcomes.text: Students identify a problem and create a business idea using design thinking
Students will use digital tools to create and present a business plan
Additional SLO: Students will be able to analyze constructs and fundamentals of textual (syntax-based) programming.
Students will be able to understand and describe number systems and encoding schemes for data representation in computer systems
Students will be able to explain how system software controls the flow of information between hardware components used for input, output, storage, and processing
Students will identify and learn common software tools such as translators, integrated development environments, online and offline computing platforms, code repositories, etc.
Students will identify common algorithms used to develop software, store, search, or sort information
Develop and apply abstractions to create generalized, modular solutions
Students should be able to differentiate between front-end development, and back-end development of a website
Students should be able to use more advanced HTML/CSS features in an appropriate environment
Students should be able to use more advanced programming constructs (lists, etc.) to create dynamic websites using JavaScript as backend scripting
Students should be able to implement complex algorithms that use more complex data structures (lists, etc.) in JavaScript
Students will determine more advanced techniques (unit tests, breakpoints, watches) for testing and debugging their code in JavaScript

subtopics.title: Data science, AI and data visualization

outcomes.text: Students will understand and explain the scope of data science, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML), including types of supervised and unsupervised learning models, and their applications to common real-world problems.
Students will understand and explain the types, uses, and methods of data visualizations and understand the benefits of visualizing data
Students will be able to apply stages of the data science life cycle e.g. understanding a real-world business problem, data gathering, building model, interpreting results).

units.title: Domain E: Applications of Computer Science

topics.title: Domain E: Applications of Computer Science

outcomes.text: Students will be able to describe uses and applications that are enabled by technologies like IoT, and Blockchain
Students will be able to explain that AI can be applied to specific applications in areas like NLP, Robotics, Speech Recognition, etc.
Students will be able to demonstrate the social implications of AI

subtopics.title: Internet safety, cyberbullying and the digital divide

outcomes.text: Understand and apply safe & responsible use of the internet to prevent addiction, promote information and data security
Evaluate the impact of and apply strategies to prevent cyberbullying/harassment
Analyze the impacts of the digital divide on access to critical information

subtopics.title: Communicating and publishing with digital tools

outcomes.text: Communicate and publish key ideas and details to a variety of audiences using appropriate digital tools and media-rich resources

units.title: Domain H: Entrepreneurship in the Digital Age

topics.title: Domain H: Entrepreneurship in the Digital Age

outcomes.text: Students will use digital tools to conduct research to collect market and customer insights for a business idea
Students will pitch a business idea
Students will be able to understand and apply logic gates in digital systems, define and create truth tables using Boolean operators like AND, OR, NOT, NAND, XOR) and logic diagrams

Students will be able to understand and evaluate stages of the systems design, e.g. software development life cycle (analysis, design, coding, and testing etc.), and software development methodologies
Students will be able to understand and explain the scalability and reliability of networking systems via network topology
Understand and explain the need for cybersecurity and contrast different methods of encryption to transmit data
Plan, develop, systematically test, and refine computational artifacts for problem-solving such as pseudocode, etc.
Apply common search, and sort algorithms
Students should understand the importance of computer programming and applications
Students should be able to write and execute simple programs in Python.
Students should be able to draw shapes using Turtle Graphics functions in Python
Students should be able to understand the need for libraries and learn the use of some simple libraries in Python.

subtopics.title: Algorithms, functions and debugging in Python

outcomes.text: Students should be able to translate simple algorithms that use sequence and repetition in Python.
Students should be able to decompose a problem into sub-problems and implement those sub-problems using functions in Python.
Students will determine ways of debugging their code in Python

subtopics.title: Model building, experimental design and summary statistics

outcomes.text: Students will be able to relate the role and importance of model building with their real-world applications
Students will understand and explain experimental design in data science
Students will analyze pre-existing datasets to create summary statistics and data visuals (such as bar charts, pie charts, line graphs, etc.)

units.title: Domain E: Applications of Computer Science

topics.title: Domain E: Applications of Computer Science

subtopics.title: IoT, cloud computing, blockchain and AI design

outcomes.text: Students should be able to describe technologies that are the foundations of IoT systems, Cloud Computing, and Blockchain
Students should be able to evaluate how different stakeholder's culture, values, and (sometimes conflicting) interests affect AI System designs.
Understand and apply safe & responsible use of information sources, identifying sources of reliable information compared to unreliable information and its sources
Define and discuss how computing has increased connectivity by enabling communication between people and the environmental, cultural, and human impact of increased connectivity
Perform advanced searches to locate information and/or design a data-collection approach to gather original data (e.g., qualitative interviews, surveys, prototypes, simulations)

units.title: Domain H: Entrepreneurship in the Digital Age

topics.title: Domain H: Entrepreneurship in the Digital Age

outcomes.text: Students will create, test, and iterate a prototype for a business idea
Students will explain the usability, security and accessibility of devices, the systems they are integrated with.
Explain human interaction with computer systems in terms of: Usability; Common problems; Methods for improvements; Ethical, social, economic, and environmental implications
Identify and explain tradeoffs between the usability and security of computing systems, recommend cybersecurity measures by considering different factors such as efficiency, cost, privacy, and ethics
Understand and evaluate the computational solutions in terms of efficiency, clarity, and correctness
Understand and apply complex algorithms on data structures such as trees and binary search
Students should be able to understand and evaluate applications of various programming paradigms.
Students should be able to use more advanced programming constructs such as data structures (lists etc.), file handling (disk IO to write to storage), and databases in Python.
Students should be able to implement complex algorithms that use lists etc. in Python
Students will determine more advanced techniques (unit tests, breakpoints, watches) for testing and debugging their code in Python

subtopics.title: Model performance, visualization and hypothesis testing

outcomes.text: Students will be able to analyse data and identify key model performance metrics of real-world machine learning models.
Students will explain and create a data visualization using Structured Query Language (SQL), or Python, or R
Advanced SLO: Students will learn how to form hypotheses and perform hypothesis testing. Students will learn to communicate findings using advanced data visuals and tie them back to hypotheses.

topics.title: Domain E: Applications of Computer Science

subtopics.title: Applications for Pakistan, deep learning and AI policy

outcomes.text: Students should be able to design ideas of applications relevant to Pakistan using IoT, Cloud computing, and Blockchain
Students should be able to describe deep learning and its applications
Students should be able to assess policies that can help protect different stakeholders' interests
Students should be able to evaluate scenarios with data sharing and privacy conflicts and suggest policy decisions that can help achieve acceptable compromises.

subtopics.title: Safe collaboration, security threats and equity

outcomes.text: Identify and apply safe practices when collaborating on digital or online platforms.
Discuss security threats and mitigation such as 2FA, biometric verification, and secure techniques for transmitting data etc.
Collaborate on strategies to provide equity and equal access to information
Students will create an artifact that answers a research question, communicates results and conclusions through digital resources or tools
